name: Torino Cherokee (Turismo Carretera)
hook: In 2017 the Torinos won eight of the fifteen Turismo Carretera races and still lost the title, by a quarter of a point.
story: Picture Argentina's oldest racing series, the Turismo Carretera. For years the fight has been Ford against Chevrolet. But there is a third name on the grid, and its road car went out of production in 1982. Torino. It was Argentina's own muscle coupé, born in the sixties. The race car keeps that long, low shape and carries a Jeep Cherokee straight-six, first raced in 1995. In 2017 the Torinos are flying. They win eight of the season's fifteen races. Facundo Ardusso, driving for the Renault Sport Torino Team, arrives at the final round in La Plata fighting for the title. Then Agustín Canapino's Chevrolet goes to work. He starts eleventh. Lap by lap he climbs. On the very last lap he takes fourth. Now the sums are done. Canapino is champion by a quarter of a point, the smallest margin the series has ever seen. Torino's long wait for a title goes on. Think about that. The car that won more than half the races, beaten by a fraction you could barely write down.
description: The Torino Cherokee is the Turismo Carretera racer that carries the shape of the IKA Torino, the Argentine coupé built from 1966 to 1982. It is developed under the rules of the ACTC, the association that runs the series, and takes its name from its engine: a Jeep Cherokee inline-six, first homologated in the Torino in 1995 and later shared with Dodge. In 2017 Torinos won eight of the fifteen races, and Facundo Ardusso finished runner-up by 0.25 points.
